title: How to Choose Your Starting Seeds
summary: Understand the vital difference between industrial F1 hybrid seeds and reproducible open-pollinated seeds, to start your production on solid and sustainable foundations.

pages.title: The First Seed Decides Everything
pages.text:
Producing your own seeds requires work and care.
For your efforts to bear fruit, you must start with a seed capable of reproducing faithfully year after year.
In this module, you will discover how to choose your starting seeds without falling into the trap of industrial seeds.
pages.illustration_description: Plan moyen : deux mains paysannes comparant deux sachets de semences : un sachet industriel brillant avec code-barres et mention "F1", et une bourse en tissu traditionnel marquée à la main "Variété locale reproductible".

pages.title: What is an F1 hybrid seed?
pages.text:
In stores or cooperatives, many seed packets bear the mention **"F1 Hybrid"**.
These seeds are created by industrial producers by forcibly crossing two very inbred lines.
In the first year, the plants grow quickly and produce fruits that are all identical.
But it's a trap for the following year!
pages.illustration_description: Laboratoire industriel schématique : croisement forcé entre deux plantes fragiles donnant une graine mise dans un sachet commercial avec la mention "Hybride F1" entourée d'un cadenas.

pages.title: The F2 Harvest Trap
pages.text:
If you harvest seeds from an F1 fruit to replant them the following year (what is called the **F2 generation**):
❌ The plants lose their vigor.
❌ Some fruits are small, others tasteless or diseased.
❌ Many seeds are sterile.
The farmer is then forced to buy new seeds every season!
pages.illustration_description:
Comparaison en 2 saisons :
- Saison 1 (F1) : rangée de légumes bien alignés et uniformes.
- Saison 2 (F2) : rangée très inégale, plantes rabougries, fruits difformes avec points de maladie et croix rouges ❌.

pages.title: The Farmer's Financial Dependence
pages.text:
Buying F1 seeds every year is very expensive.
This makes the producer dependent on stores, transportation, and multinational corporations.
If borders close or prices rise, the farmer can no longer sow their land.
Freedom begins when you don't depend on anyone for your seeds!
pages.illustration_description: Dessin expressif : un paysan tendant son porte-monnaie vide vers un comptoir commercial, avec une chaîne symbolique brisée lorsqu'il tient dans son autre main ses propres graines paysannes.

pages.title: Farmer Seeds: A Reproducible Treasure
pages.text:
In contrast, **farmer seeds** (also known as landraces or local seeds) reproduce faithfully from one generation to the next.
When you sow the seeds you have harvested:
✅ They yield vigorous and flavorful plants.
✅ They belong to everyone, without patents or restrictions on replanting.
pages.illustration_description: Une famille paysanne souriante récoltant d'abondants légumes dans son champ, avec un symbole infini (∞) reliant les graines récoltées aux semis de la saison suivante.

pages.title: A Seed Adapted to Your Real Climate
pages.text:
Industrial seeds were created to grow with chemical fertilizers and abundant water.
Local **heirloom varieties**, on the other hand, have faced the scorching sun, poor soils, and diseases of your region for decades.
They know how to resist **drought** and withstand **heatwaves**!
pages.illustration_description:
Deux plantes face au soleil brûlant :
- À gauche : variété industrielle assoiffée, flétrie malgré le soleil ❌.
- À droite : variété paysanne locale, feuilles bien vertes, racines profondes qui descendent chercher l'eau dans le sol sec ✅.

pages.title: Where to find good starter seeds?
pages.text:
To build your initial seed stock:
1. Ask elders and reputable market gardeners in your village or neighboring villages.
2. Participate in farmers' seed fairs and seed exchanges.
3. Get in touch with local farmer seed associations or agroecological farms.
pages.illustration_description: Scène conviviale sous l'arbre à palabres : échange amical de petites bourses de graines entre paysans de différentes générations, avec des sourires et des poignées de main chaleureuses.

pages.title: Choosing Seeds from Agroecology
pages.text:
Always prioritize seeds multiplied without chemical fertilizers or synthetic pesticides.

A plant accustomed to the crutch of chemical products becomes lazy.

A seed born in living soil (with compost and mulching) will produce autonomous and vibrant plants.
pages.illustration_description: Coupe de sol maraîcher riche : paillage de paille, vers de terre actifs, racines saines d'une plante nourrie au compost naturel avec un grand papillon butinant au-dessus.

pages.title: Observe the health of the seed lot before adopting
pages.text:
When you are given or sold a seed lot, inspect it carefully:
- The seeds must be whole, without small weevil holes ⚠️.
- No traces of gray or white mold or rancid odor ❌.
- No excessive dirt (pieces of stones, leaf debris, wild grass seeds).
pages.illustration_description:
Gros plan sur une calebasse contenant des graines tamisées et propres sous une loupe :
- Coche verte sur les graines lisses et brillantes ✅
- Croix rouge sur deux graines trouées ou noircies ❌.

pages.title: Learn about the variety's history
pages.text:
Always ask a few questions to the person giving you the seeds:
- "How long does it take from sowing to the first harvest?"
- "How does it perform during the dry season or heavy rains?"
- "What is the taste, texture when cooked, and storage life of the vegetable?"
Note these valuable answers in your notebook!
pages.illustration_description: Un jeune maraîcher tenant un carnet et un crayon, écoutant attentivement les explications d'un paysan expérimenté au milieu des cultures.

pages.title: Start Small and Test First
pages.text:
Don't change all your plots at once with a variety you don't know yet!

**The first season:**
- Sow a small test bed (a few dozen plants).
- Observe its behavior on your own land.
- If the result is good, harvest the seeds to expand the crop the following season.
pages.illustration_description: Plan de jardin montrant une petite planche test bien étiquetée "Test variété locale" à côté des cultures habituelles du jardinier.

pages.title: Share to Multiply
pages.text:
Nature is generous: a single fruit often yields dozens, even hundreds of seeds!
You will quickly have far more seeds than you need for your own consumption.
Give and exchange your surplus with your neighbors:
- The more a variety is grown in the region, the less likely it is to disappear!
pages.illustration_description: Trois maraîchers se partageant des sachets de semences avec enthousiasme. Des flèches connectent les trois fermes formant un réseau de solidarité semencière.

pages.title: What to absolutely avoid
pages.text:
To preserve your autonomy:

❌ Never harvest seeds from market-bought vegetables without knowing their origin (often from treated F1 hybrids).
❌ Do not start with seeds treated with toxic colored chemical powders.
❌ Do not save seeds from plots where a severe viral disease was present.
pages.illustration_description:
Trois signaux d'alerte barrés d'un grand cercle rouge d'interdiction :
1. Légumes anonymes du supermarché
2. Graines enrobées de poudre chimique rouge ou rose fluo
3. Feuille de tomate rabougrie et tachetée de virus.

pages.title: Your Seed Grower's Notebook
pages.text:
From your very first day of seed harvesting, keep a small notebook.
Write down:
- The name of the person who gave you the initial seed
- The date of receipt
- Remarkable qualities observed during the season
This is the living memory of your farm!
pages.illustration_description: Cahier d'écolier simple posé sur une planche en bois, avec une belle écriture manuscrite et un petit échantillon de graines scotché sur le coin de la page.

pages.title: Congratulations! You hold the keys to independence
pages.text:
Bravo! You've taken the step towards food sovereignty:
✅ You know how to avoid the trap of F1 hybrid seeds
✅ You prioritize local and reproducible varieties
✅ You know how to check the health of your starting seeds

Next module: understanding pollination and fertilization of flowers in the vegetable garden!
pages.illustration_description:
Le maraîcher regarde l'horizon avec confiance, tenant dans ses mains une belle récolte variée et colorée.
Bannière flottante avec le slogan : "Semences paysannes : autonomie, liberté et abondance !".
